across_options.issue: Phone frame width and aspect ratio vary: approximately 744, 750 and 738 image pixels wide respectively, all at 1536 high. At equal phone width the content therefore has different vertical positions and proportions. This violates the one-axis comparison in brand/constitution.md Art. 14.4.

C changes spacing and card geometry: card edges are around x166–858 versus A x170–855 and B x169–855; its second card begins around y819 versus y810 in A/B. Its navigation divider rises to about y1392 versus y1403 in A/B. These are layout changes, not D2 typeface changes (brand/constitution.md Art. 14.4; brand/ledger.md D3).

The item photographs are not held fixed. Jacket shape, folds and framing change, particularly in C; the shoes and their crop also differ. This adds an imagery variable to the D2 comparison (brand/constitution.md Art. 14.4).

The field coloration/line texture and lime amount-band color vary between boards. The amount band also has different bounds, about x188–491 in A, x186–473 in B and x184–477 in C. A and B share the same declared text face, so their amount/band width change is not explained by the named typeface pairing. These introduce field and money-treatment differences beyond D2 (brand/constitution.md Art. 14.4; brand/ledger.md D5 and D6).
